active_problem.root_problem: Billing dispute tickets have roughly doubled since August 2026 (from ~600/month in Jun-Jul to 1180-1260/month in Aug-Sep, E-06), and the dominant driver is a billing import/validation defect producing incorrect bills on ACTUAL-read accounts rather than ticket-response speed (E-01 shows response times within SLA) or estimated-read substitution from field/AMI issues (E-04 shows disputed bills are dominated by ACTUAL reads, 1785 vs 1240 ESTIMATED, and E-03 rules out a tariff change). interpretation_history.interpretation: CRM data (2440 tickets) shows median response time 1.6 days and p90 2.8 days, both inside the 3.0-day SLA, indicating ticket-handling speed is not currently a measurable gap in how disputes are being answered.

Route-log data (E-02) shows manual-read route completion of 88% against a 95% target, covering 9200 manual-read accounts, during the Aug-Sep 2026 period that matches the dispute surge window — a measurable shortfall in field meter-read collection, not yet linked to disputes directly.

Billing-db's tariff change log returned zero records, indicating no tariff rate changes occurred in the relevant period — ruling out a tariff-rate change as a cause of incorrect bills, independent of the billing import validation rule question.

release_summary.summary: Customer Service (SH-CS) reported dispute tickets roughly doubled since August and asked for an AI agent to auto-answer tickets and "fix whatever is causing wrong bills" (CL-01). Investigation ruled out slow ticket handling (E-01: within SLA) and a tariff change (E-03, E-05, CL-02). An initial problem framing (PD-1@v1) attributed the surge mainly to ACTUAL-read billing errors, but was invalidated when MDMS data (E-12) showed the 1240 ESTIMATED-read disputes (matching E-04) are actually caused by billing-import rejections (REJECTED_HIGH_CONSUMPTION) of valid AMI reads, not field/AMI delivery failure. Follow-up evidence confirmed the mechanism: validation rule BV-17, deployed 2026-08-01 (E-13), compares raw AMI register values to a 12-month m3 history with unit_scaling='none', while v4.2-firmware meters report in 0.1 m3 units rather than m3 (E-14), causing valid high-consumption reads to be misclassified and rejected (1184 of 1240 cases). The successor problem (PD-1@v2) was defined around this confirmed mechanism, but whether it also explains the larger ACTUAL-read dispute population (1785) is unresolved (VOB-U-ACTUAL-READ-MECHANISM, open), as is whether Billing Operations has authority to correct BV-17 (VOB-U-RULE-CORRECTION-AUTHORITY, open). The actual fix (SR-FIX-BV17-UNIT-SCALING) could not be deployed within remaining contest time. The release decision is RELEASE_WITH_KNOWN_LIMITATION: only a dispute-volume trend monitoring deliverable (monitor_dispute_volume_trend:DA-TICKET) is released, with no automated bill writes or rule changes, while the unresolved mechanism, authority, and fix-deployment gaps are documented as explicit limitations.
key_points: Dispute volume rose from ~600/month (Jun-Jul, E-06) to 1180-1260/month (Aug-Sep, E-06); ticket response time stayed within SLA (E-01) and no tariff change occurred (E-03, E-05, CL-02), ruling those out as causes.

The 1240 ESTIMATED-read disputed bills (E-04) correspond to AMI read events: 1184 were valid reads rejected at billing import as REJECTED_HIGH_CONSUMPTION, and 56 had no AMI read received at all (E-12).

Validation rule BV-17, deployed 2026-08-01, compares raw register values to a 12-month m3 history with unit_scaling='none' (E-13); v4.2 meters (rolled out 2026-06) report in 0.1 m3 units, not m3 (E-14) — the confirmed mechanism for the 1184 rejections (hypothesis H-HIGH-CONSUMPTION-REJECTION-R, CONFIRMED).

Field-reader staffing shortage (SH-FIELD's claim, CL-03/E-07) and route completion shortfall (E-02, 88% vs 95% target) were assessed as at most a secondary factor, since the dominant ESTIMATED-dispute driver is the billing-import rejection, not field/AMI delivery failure.

Whether the BV-17 unit mismatch (or a related issue) also explains the larger ACTUAL-read dispute population (1785, E-04) remains unconfirmed (VOB-U-ACTUAL-READ-MECHANISM, CRITICAL, OPEN) and is outside this release's scope.
Whether Billing Operations (SH-BILL) holds authority to correct the BV-17 rule configuration is unconfirmed (VOB-U-RULE-CORRECTION-AUTHORITY, HIGH, OPEN) and is outside this release's scope.

The released scope is limited to monitor_dispute_volume_trend:DA-TICKET; no billing-config, billing-db bill, or field-dispatch write actions are included, consistent with K-BILLWRITE and K-DISPATCH constraints and success criteria SC-NO-AUTOMATED-BILL-WRITES / SC-NO-RULE-WRITE.

The identified remedy to fix the root cause (SR-FIX-BV17-UNIT-SCALING, removes_root_cause=true) requires normal billing-config change management by SH-BILL and could not be deployed and observed within the remaining contest time budget.
limitations_explained: This release does not claim a confirmed mechanism for the 1785 ACTUAL-read disputes; the confirmed root-cause mechanism (unit-scaling rejection) is established only for the 1240 ESTIMATED-read population.
No actual billing correction occurs in this release: the fix for BV-17's unit mismatch exists as a proposal (SR-FIX-BV17-UNIT-SCALING) but was not deployed or observed, so bills remain uncorrected.
Dispute-volume trend monitoring itself has reduced confidence because the completeness of the underlying CRM ticket data (DA-TICKET) is recorded as UNKNOWN.

The DEFINE Gate result was CONDITIONAL_PASS, meaning some items were deferred rather than fully resolved before definition closed; they are tracked as open verification obligations (VOBs) rather than settled facts.

Two critical/high-impact questions remain open and are explicitly excluded from this release's scope: whether the same billing defect explains ACTUAL-read disputes, and whether Billing Operations has authority to correct the BV-17 rule.

The release decision is RELEASE_WITH_KNOWN_LIMITATION: only a dispute-volume trend monitoring deliverable (monitor_dispute_volume_trend:DA-TICKET) is released, with no automated bill writes or rule changes, while the unresolved mechanism, authority, and fix-deployment gaps are documented as explicit limitations.

The 1240 ESTIMATED-read disputed bills (E-04) correspond to AMI read events: 1184 were valid reads rejected at billing import as REJECTED_HIGH_CONSUMPTION, and 56 had no AMI read received at all (E-12).

Validation rule BV-17, deployed 2026-08-01, compares raw register values to a 12-month m3 history with unit_scaling='none' (E-13); v4.2 meters (rolled out 2026-06) report in 0.1 m3 units, not m3 (E-14) — the confirmed mechanism for the 1184 rejections (hypothesis H-HIGH-CONSUMPTION-REJECTION-R, CONFIRMED).
